cues.en: So I'm going to go through today and talk to you about my five key points of building a healthy soil. The first is the least amount of mechanical disturbance possible. And I'm doing that in a no-till situation. I realize organic producers are going to till some, just make your tillage minimal. This slide was put together and it really illustrates the destruction of tillage. This farmer had a forested area.
cues.zh: 今天我来给大家讲讲构建健康土壤的五个关键点。第一点是尽可能减少机械扰动。我是在免耕条件下做到这一点的。我知道有机农户多少会翻耕，但请尽量减到最少。这张幻灯片非常直观地展现了翻耕的破坏性。这位农户原本有一片林地。

cues.en: and he cleared part of that area, farmed it intensive tillage, monoculture soybeans for 17 years. And look what happened. That's a picture of the forested area soils and then the field that he cleared. What you see is a decrease in organic matter from 4.3 down to 1.6% with 17 years of tillage.
cues.zh: 他开垦了其中一部分，采用集约翻耕、单一连作大豆种了17年。看看结果如何。这张照片对比了林地土壤和他开垦后的农田。可以看到，经过17年的翻耕，有机质从4.3%骤降到了1.6%。

cues.en: I wish I would have had the foresight back in 1991 when I bought that place to archive some of the soils, because I'll guarantee you, they look like the soils on your right there. They were compacted. There was no life in them. As I said, we were down to less than 2% organic matter. We had taken the life out of those soils. No-till is a big part of that. And no-till will work anywhere in the world there's production agriculture. I've seen it. It works.
cues.zh: 真希望我1991年买下那个农场时有远见能留些土壤样本，因为我敢保证，当时的地就像右边照片里那样。土壤板结，毫无生机。正如我所说，有机质降到了不足2%。我们榨干了那些土壤的生命力。免耕是扭转这一局面的关键。只要世界上有农业生产的地方，免耕就一定管用。我亲眼见证过，它确实有效。

cues.en: And it's key to building healthy soils. The other thing that's key is to take advantage of the natural things that occur in healthy soils, untilled soils. And one of those is mycorrhizal fungi. And I'm not a scientist, so I'm not going to get real in depth with that. But we don't take advantage of the natural processes that occur in our soil. Mycorrhizal fungi will form a symbiotic relationship with the roots.
cues.zh: 这对于构建健康土壤至关重要。另一个关键是利用健康、未经翻耕的土壤中天然存在的生物，其中之一就是菌根真菌。我不是科学家，不会讲得太深奥。但我们往往没有充分利用土壤中发生的自然过程。菌根真菌会与植物根系形成共生关系。

cues.en: And what it more or less is doing is it's extending the system, the root network of that plant. So that plant is able to gather and store nutrients and water from a much bigger area. Well, when we till, we destroy this. If we have untilled soils and promote healthy soils, we're going to get more mycorrhizal fungi, and we're going to be able to take advantage of that. And I'll show you some pictures coming up of just how important that is.
cues.zh: 它本质上是在扩展植物的根系网络，让植物能从更广阔的区域收集和储存养分及水分。但一旦翻耕，就会破坏这一切。如果我们实行免耕、促进土壤健康，就会有更多的菌根真菌，并能从中受益。接下来我会展示一些照片，说明这到底有多重要。

cues.en: The other thing mycorrhizal fungi can do, when it gets into that host plant's roots, it'll prevent pathogens and nematodes from entering that root cell wall. So we can actually decrease the amount of fungicides, et cetera, that we have to put on our crops because we're taking advantage of this natural ecosystem process.
cues.zh: 菌根真菌的另一个作用是，当它进入寄主植物根系后，能阻止病原体和线虫侵入根细胞壁。这样一来，利用这种自然生态过程，我们其实就能减少作物上杀菌剂等农药的使用量。

cues.en: The other thing mycorrhizal fungi does is it starts soil formation. Think back to that picture I showed there with the 17 years of tillage in soybeans. There's no soil aggregates in that picture. The soil aggregates are being destroyed. Mycorrhizal fungi secretes a glue called glomalin, and aclomalin then is a sticky substance that starts soil formation. So the picture on the left there, that's soil particles being formed.
cues.zh: 菌根真菌还能启动土壤结构的形成。回想一下我刚才展示的种了17年大豆的翻耕照片，图里根本没有土壤团聚体，它们全被破坏了。菌根真菌会分泌一种叫球囊霉素的胶质，这种黏性物质正是土壤团聚形成的起点。左边那张照片展示的就是正在形成的土壤颗粒。

cues.en: due to the glow melon secreted by mycorrhizal fungi. Here's what some of our soils look like today. After 21 years of no-till and everything else, I'm going to talk to you about today, but notice that soil aggregation. That's what we want soils to look like. Soils should look like black cottage cheese, full of carbon, full of pore spaces, and that aggregation. Mycorrhizal fungi do a lot of things. They improve aggregate stability,
cues.zh: 这是菌根真菌分泌的球囊霉素带来的。这是我们目前一部分土壤的样貌。经过 21 年的免耕，以及我今天将要跟你们讲的所有措施，注意看那些土壤团聚体。这就是我们希望土壤呈现的样子。土壤应该像黑色的乡村奶酪一样，富含有机碳，充满孔隙，还有那种团聚结构。菌根真菌的作用非常多。它们能提高团聚体稳定性，

cues.en: They build soil carbon, they improve the water use efficiency, and they increase the efficiency of nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulfur. And if we're adding especially phosphorus to our farming practices, that's actually detrimental to mycorrhizal fungi. Ways to increase it, reduce or eliminate chemical use, reduce or eliminate tillage, reduce or eliminate synthetic fertilizers,
cues.zh: 增加土壤碳含量，提高水分利用效率，并提升氮、磷、硫的利用效率。如果我们耕作时额外施磷肥，实际上对菌根真菌是有害的。增加菌根真菌的方法包括：减少或停用化学品，减少或杜绝耕翻，减少或停止使用化肥，

cues.en: and they have a living plant root in the ground as long as possible. These are things we can accomplish both in our perennial systems and in our annual cropping systems. It can be done, and I'm going to show you how we've done that. In 2003, I was fortunate, Dr. Chris Nichols there. She did some of the original work when Glomaland was discovered by Dr. Sarah Wright. She was a grad student under Dr. Sarah Wright.
cues.zh: 以及尽可能让活的植物根系留在地里。这些在我们多年生系统和一年生耕作系统中都能实现。这是完全可行的，我也会向大家展示我们是如何做到的。2003 年我很幸运，结识了那边的 Dr. Chris Nichols。当 Dr. Sarah Wright 发现球囊霉素时，她就参与了早期的研究。她当时是 Dr. Sarah Wright 的研究生。

cues.en: Dr. Nichols came to the ARS lab in Mandan, North Dakota. In 2003, she came out to my place, looked at what I was doing, and she said, Gabe, you've come a long ways, but your soils will never be sustainable unless you remove your synthetic fertilizer input. And I thought, wow, how can I farm without synthetic fertilizer? So for the next four years, we did split trials on our operation. We took fields, and half the field would use synthetic fertilizer.
cues.zh: Dr. Nichols 后来去了北达科他州 Mandan 的 ARS 实验室。2003 年，她来到我的农场，看我做的事情，她说：“Gabe，你已经走了很远，但除非你停用化肥，否则你的土壤永远无法实现可持续。”当时我想，天啊，不用化肥我还怎么种地？于是在接下来的四年里，我们在农场做了对照试验。我们划分了地块，一半使用化肥，

cues.en: or the other half we want. All four years, the non-fertilized tracts were equal to or greater in yield than the fertilized tracts. So we haven't used any synthetic fertilizers on our operation since 2008. How has that affected our yield? Our yields are over 25% higher than the county average. Am I the highest in the county? No. Am I the most profitable? Yes. Simple as that. But you have to get your soils healthy
cues.zh: 另一半则不用。整整四年，未施化肥地块的产量都等于甚至超过了施肥地块。因此，从 2008 年起，我们的农场就再也没用过任何化肥。这对我们的产量有什么影响呢？我们的产量比全县平均水平高出 25% 以上。我是全县产量最高的吗？不是。我是利润最高的吗？是的。就这么简单。但你必须先让土壤恢复健康，

cues.en: First, and I'm in no way standing here to tell you to immediately eliminate synthetic fertilizer. You're going to have a disaster if you do. You need to, it's like a drug addict, you need to wean it off slowly. But once you build that population of soil biology, build that healthy mycorrhizal fungi population, you will be able to drastically reduce your synthetic fertilizer inputs. Okay, the second principle of a healthy soil is armor on the soil surface.
cues.zh: 首先，我绝不是站在这里让大家立刻停用化肥。要是直接停用，结果会是灾难性的。这就像戒瘾一样，你得循序渐进地戒掉。但只要你建立起土壤生物群落，培育出健康的菌根真菌种群，你就能够大幅削减化肥的投入。好，健康土壤的第二个原则，就是地表覆盖保护。

cues.en: Look at perennial native range, always covered all the time. Bare soil is a detriment to soil health. I think back to my father-in-law telling me, the more you work the soil, the better it is. That is not the way nature works. Where in nature do you find bare soil? Only where there was a catastrophic event or where man imposed his will on it. This is what happens when we till. This is eastern Colorado just this past January.
cues.zh: 看看多年生原生草场，它始终都被植被覆盖着。裸露的土壤对土壤健康是种破坏。我回想起岳父曾对我说：地耕得越多越好。但大自然可不是这么运作的。你在大自然里哪里见过裸土？只有在遭遇灾害，或者人类强行干预的地方才有。这就是耕作的后果。这是今年一月的科罗拉多州东部。

cues.en: You'd think it was back out of the 30s and out of the Dust Bowl. Not so. You would have thought we would have learned something in the past 80-plus years. Evidently, we haven't. Last Father's Day, my son said, dad, for Father's Day, I'm going to take you there having a soil health tour. This is what we took a picture of on that soil health tour. It was an operation with tillage. I don't see much soil health in that photo. This is what it looks like on our operation. That's a seeded field.
cues.zh: 你可能会以为这是倒退回了30年代的“黑风暴”时期。其实并不是。按理说这80多年来我们早该吸取教训了。但显然，我们并没有。去年父亲节，我儿子说：爸，父亲节我带你去个地方，那边有个土壤健康考察活动。这就是我们在那次考察中拍下的照片。那是一个采用耕作模式的农场。从照片里我可没看出土壤有多健康。而这是我们农场的样子。那是已经播种的田地。

cues.en: We want armor on the soil surface. We want that soil covered at all times. Here's a cover crop emerging through that armor on the surface. How are weeds going to germinate there? I'm able to save on herbicides. Because we have that armor, weeds aren't going to germinate through that, but the crop does just fine. That residue also buffers our heat. Now, we can get hot, not as hot as you get here.
cues.zh: 我们希望土壤表面有一层“铠甲”。我们希望土壤始终被覆盖着。看这里，覆盖作物正穿透表层的铠甲破土而出。杂草怎么可能在那儿发芽？这样我就能省下除草剂的钱。因为有了这层铠甲，杂草穿不透它发芽，但农作物却长得非常好。那些残茬还能起到隔热缓冲的作用。我们那儿有时也很热，虽然比不上你们这里。

cues.en: in southern Idaho, but we can get pretty hot in August. That heat is detrimental to soil life. Here we had a tour out on our place, and we stuck this thermometer in on your left. That's where the cover crop is. It was almost 100 degrees outside that day, and that thermometer registered 87.6 degrees. On bare soil, 107 degrees. That 20 degree temperature difference is huge.
cues.zh: 在爱达荷州南部，八月份会变得相当热。这种高温对土壤生命是致命的。之前有人来我们农场参观，我们把温度计插在大家左手边的地里。那是种植了覆盖作物的地方。那天室外温度接近100度，而温度计显示的土温是87.6度。但在裸露土壤上，温度高达107度。这20度的温差极其悬殊。

cues.en: What's the effect of temperature on soil life and on plant growth? At 70 degrees soil temp, 100% of the moisture is used for growth. Once we get to 100 degrees, only 15% of that is used for plant growth. So go back to this photo. In other words, if I don't have armor on the soil surface, my plants aren't going to produce. They're not going to grow anymore. But where I have armor, I'm still getting growth out of my plants. That equates to dollars in my pocket.
cues.zh: 温度对土壤生命和植物生长有什么影响？在土温70度时，100%的水分都会用于生长。一旦达到100度，就只有15%的水分用于植物生长了。所以再回到这张照片。换句话说，如果土壤表面没有铠甲，我的作物就不会有产出。它们就停止生长了。但在有铠甲覆盖的地方，我的作物依然在生长。这就等于真金白银装进了我的口袋。

cues.en: If we get much hotter than that, we start affecting soil biology. And soil biology is the key driver for the nutrient cycle that's going to provide our plants the nutrients. We need to keep those soil temperatures down. The other thing is you have armor on the soil surface and you'll have this. You'll have a lot of biology. There's more microorganisms in a teaspoon full of healthy soil than there are people on this world. Think about that.
cues.zh: 如果温度比这还要高，就会开始破坏土壤生物群。而土壤生物群是养分循环的核心驱动力，负责为植物提供养分。我们必须把土壤温度降下来。另一方面，只要土壤表面有了铠甲，你就会拥有这些——拥有丰富的生物群。一茶匙健康的土壤里，微生物的数量比全世界的人口还要多。想想看吧。

cues.en: Yet how often as producers do we think about feeding that soil biology? How often do we think about protecting it, keeping armor on the soil surface? We need to do that. That's the residue brushed away in the cover crop. I know it's hard to see here, but that's solid earthworm castings. When we bought that farm in 1991, I tell people I could never take a day off and go fishing because you wouldn't find an earthworm on the whole farm.
cues.zh: 但作为农场主，我们有多少次考虑过去喂养土壤中的生物呢？又有多少次想过保护它、给土壤表面披上一层铠甲？我们必须这么做。拨开覆盖作物的残留物，我知道这里看不太清楚，但这些全都是实打实的蚯蚓粪。1991年我们买下那个农场时，我总跟别人讲，我根本没法休假去钓鱼，因为整个农场连一条蚯蚓都找不着。

cues.en: Last spring we did earthworm counts. 12 inches, 12 inches, 2 inches deep. We were averaging over 60. That's a lot of earthworms. I never transplanted any, didn't bring any in. They came on their own. Build it and they will come. But you have to provide the home for them first. Third principle of building a healthy soil is diversity. Look at true native rangeland. This photo here is from one of our native rangeland pastures. And I tell people I bought that land
cues.zh: 去年春天我们做了蚯蚓计数。长宽各12英寸，深2英寸。平均能数出60多条。这蚯蚓可真够多的。我从来没移植过，也没从外面带过一条进来。它们都是自己来的。建好巢穴，它们自然会来。但你得先给它们准备好家园。构建健康土壤的第三个原则是多样性。看看真正的原生草场吧。这张照片就是我们其中一块原生牧场。我常跟人说，我买下那块地……

cues.en: A number of years ago, I bought it for two reasons. Number one, because it was true healthy native range that hadn't been disturbed. My son teaches range management at the local community college. He brought his class out to this particular paddock, and in two hours, they counted over 140 different species of grasses, forbs, and legumes. That's diversity. If we have that type of diversity in a healthy native range, why don't we have it on our cropland?
cues.zh: 几年前我买下它有两个原因。第一，因为它是真正健康、未受打扰的原生草场。我儿子在当地社区学院教草场管理。他带班上的学生来到这片放牧地，两小时内，他们统计出了140多种不同的禾草、阔叶草和豆科植物。这就是多样性。如果健康的天然草场有这样的多样性，那为什么我们的农田里不能有呢？

cues.en: The other reason I bought this pasture was simply because with that many rocks, I'd never be tempted to break it up. In 2006, I had the opportunity to speak at a conference and this gentleman was there, Dr. Adamir Caligari from Brazil. Dr. Caligari is the world's foremost authority on cover crops. He works for the United Nations traveling all over the world. He's worked in 65 different countries and he said two things to me at that conference that really stuck out.
cues.zh: 我买下这片草场的另一个原因很简单：石头太多了，我绝不会动开垦翻地的念头。2006年，我有机会在一个会议上演讲，当时这位来自巴西的 Dr. Adamir Caligari 先生也在场。Dr. Caligari 是全球覆盖作物领域的顶级权威。他为联合国工作，走遍世界各地。他曾在65个国家工作过，在会上他跟我讲的两件事让我印象极为深刻。

cues.en: He said, you give me two inches of rainfall a year, 200 inches, or anywhere in between, and I can grow you a cover crop. Well, that told me I can do it in my dryer environment. The other thing he said is that cover crops are meant to be seeded in multi-species combinations. And I got thinking, duh, I've been using these two and three-way mixes. Dr. Caligari was talking about seven and eight and 10-way mixes.
cues.zh: 他说，不管是年降雨量2英寸、200英寸，还是介于两者之间，我都能给你种出覆盖作物。这让我明白，在更干燥的环境里我也能搞定。他说的另一件事是，覆盖作物就应该多物种组合混播。我当时就想，哎呀，我之前一直只用两三种混合。而 Dr. Caligari 谈论的可是七种、八种甚至十种的大混播。

cues.en: Think back to those native perennial ecosystems. What do you find? You find tremendous diversity. I needed to get that into my cropland. So at that time, I was on the local soil conservation district board, and we had some plotland located only a mile south of my farm. And we decided to test Dr. Caligari's wisdom there. And we were going to take and seed monoculture cover crops.
cues.zh: 回想一下那些原生多年生生态系统。你发现了什么？极其丰富的多样性。我必须把这一点带进我的农田。那时我正好是当地土壤保护区委员会的成员，我们在我农场南边仅一英里处有一块试验地。于是我们决定在那里检验 Dr. Caligari 的真知灼见。我们打算先播种单品种的覆盖作物。

cues.en: strips of them, and then at the end, we'd mix all these species together and seed a diverse polyculture and see what happened. Now, that winter was extremely dry in North Dakota. We didn't have a lot of snow, so we seeded these monocultures and this polyculture into very dry seedbed in the middle of May. These photos then, here's the plot with the cover crop growing. These photos were taken July 31st. We had less than an inch of rain on these crops.
cues.zh: 把它们按条带种下，最后把所有物种混在一起，播种多样化的混合栽培，看看会怎样。那个冬天北达科他州极度干旱。我们雪不多，所以五月中旬把这些单一栽培和混合栽培播到非常干的种床里。这些照片里，这是覆盖作物生长的小区。照片拍于7月31日。这些作物降雨不到一英寸。

cues.en: you can see the monoculture of turnips was dead. These are about approximately an acre plot each. Then you move over to the next acre, and there was the radish. That was dried up and dead. And you keep going down the line until you get to the diverse polyculture. Same soils, same seeding date, everything was the same. Look at the difference. Amazing. And that was about a 10 species mix. In other words, here they clipped it. We over tripled.
cues.zh: 可以看到芜菁单一栽培已经死了。每块大约一英亩。再移到下一英亩，是萝卜，已经干枯死亡。继续往下，直到多样化的混合栽培。同样的土壤，同样的播种日期，一切都一样。看看差别。惊人。那大约是10个物种的混合。换句话说，他们在这里剪取样方，我们的产量超过三倍。

cues.en: dry matter forage production where we had the multi-species combination. So what's happening? How can that be for all our lives? We've been told that you have to seed these monocultures, otherwise it's going to compete for moisture. That's not the way nature works. Dr. Nichols explained it best. Not only do the fungi, and she's talking about the mycorrhizal fungi, provide for the needs of one plant, but the fungal hyphae pipeline connect to multiple plants.
cues.zh: 多种物种组合下，干物质饲草产量超过三倍。那发生了什么？怎么会这样？我们一辈子都被告知必须种这些单一栽培，否则会争夺水分。自然界不是这样运作的。Nichols博士解释得最好。真菌——她说的是菌根真菌——不仅满足一株植物的需求，而且真菌菌丝网络还连接到多种植物。

cues.en: thus supplying the nutrition and moisture requirements of all the plants. So in other words, if we would seed multi-species, that mycorrhizal fungi is going to transfer nutrients and it's going to be a benefit to all the plants. Think of it this way, the rooting systems, the roots on different plants, they have different root types, different root depths. They're bringing nutrients and moisture from different areas of the soil profile.
cues.zh: 从而为所有植物提供养分和水分需求。换句话说，如果我们播种多物种，菌根真菌会转移养分，对所有植物都有益。这样想：不同植物的根系类型不同、深度不同，它们从土壤剖面的不同区域获取养分和水分。

cues.en: I spent a lot of my time talking in the Midwest, and this is what I see in the Midwest. Monoculture of corn, monoculture of beans. Remember this photo? What happens to soils under monocultures? Monocultures are a detriment to soil health. There is no doubt about it. If they weren't, then why in nature don't we find monocultures?
cues.zh: 我很多时间在中西部演讲，这就是我在中西部看到的。玉米单一栽培，豆类单一栽培。还记得这张照片吗？单一栽培下的土壤会怎样？单一栽培对土壤健康有害，毫无疑问。如果不是这样，那为什么自然界找不到单一栽培？

cues.en: So, this is what it's evolved to, and I'm jumping ahead. You know, I didn't get to this point overnight. It took a lot of years of trial and error. My son and I have a few sayings on our operation. One of them is that we want to fail every year. If we don't fail at something, we're not trying enough new things. So, I've tried a lot, hundreds of different combinations over the years, but we've gotten to the point where we no longer seed monocultures. In the upper left there, that's oats with clover growing in it.
cues.zh: 所以，这就是它演化成的样子，我有点讲快了。你知道，我不是一夜之间达到这一步的。经过了很多年的试错。我儿子和我在经营中有几句话。其中一句是，我们每年都想失败。如果我们在某件事上没有失败，说明我们尝试的新东西还不够多。所以这些年我试了很多，数百种不同组合，但我们已经到了不再播种单一栽培的地步。左上角那里，是燕麦，里面长着三叶草。

cues.en: Cool season grass, upper right is a mix of cool season broadleaves, sown as a polyculture. The lower left, that's corn with hairy vetch in it. Warm season grass along with a cool season legume. And in the lower right, that's actually sunflowers, warm season broadleaf with over 20 species of cover crops growing with it. We're trying to mimic nature. We don't do monocultures anymore on our operation.
cues.zh: 这是冷季型草，右上角是冷季型阔叶作物的混播多熟种植。左下角是玉米套种长柔毛野豌豆。暖季型禾本科草搭配冷季型豆科植物。右下角其实是向日葵，暖季型阔叶植物，伴生着 20 多种覆盖作物。我们在努力模拟自然，我们的农场不再搞单一作物种植了。

cues.en: I mentioned we have 2,000 acres of cropland on our operation. We try and get a cover crop on all 2,000 acres every year, either before a cash crop, along with a cash crop, like this case, or occasionally after the cash crop. But we want something growing at all time. Here's a close-up picture of that oats. We no longer use any synthetic fertilizers, as I mentioned. We haven't used pesticides or fungicides since before the turn of the century.
cues.zh: 我提过我们农场有 2,000 英亩耕地。我们每年都争取在所有 2,000 英亩地上种上覆盖作物，要么在经济作物之前，要么像现在这样与经济作物共生，偶尔在经济作物之后。但我们希望土地上一直有植物在生长。这是燕麦的特写照片。正如我提到的，我们不再使用任何化肥。本世纪初以来，我们就没再用过农药或杀菌剂。

cues.en: There's no need when you get a healthy soil. Nature will take care of those symptoms if you allow her to. Here's what it looks like close up. We seeded three types of clover along with the oats. We can typically get our yields of oats are in the 95 to 115 bushels without fertilizer. And when you're talking our land values, that's pretty profitable. We can make significant profit at that.
cues.zh: 土壤一旦健康，就完全没必要用那些了。只要你给大自然机会，它会解决这些问题的。这是近距离的样子。我们在燕麦间混播了三种三叶草。在不施化肥的情况下，我们的燕麦产量通常在每英亩 95 到 115 蒲式耳之间。按我们的土地成本来说，这相当赚钱，能带来很可观的利润。

cues.en: The beauty of it is we straight combine the oats off, we got that living cover. All those legumes just explode, fix nitrogen, can provide grazing for our livestock if we so desire. The fourth principle, living root in the ground as long as possible. That's where cover crops come in. And I think of cover crops as a diverse mix that enhances the life and the function of the soil, because we're really feeding all that soil biology. We're promoting that mycorrhizal fungi.
cues.zh: 妙处在于，当我们用联合收割机直接收掉燕麦后，还留着活体地被植物。所有的豆科植物迅速疯长、固氮，如果我们愿意，还能用来放牧牲畜。第四条原则是：尽可能长时间地让土壤中保留活根。这就是覆盖作物的用武之地。我认为覆盖作物是一种多样化的组合，能够提升土壤的生命力和功能，因为我们真正喂饱的是土壤生物，促进了菌根真菌的生长。

cues.en: You use cover crops to design them for what you don't have. You know, there's a big cover crop craze going on throughout the country. And I've seen a lot of disasters with cover crops because people don't plan properly. What are you trying to accomplish with that cover crop? Are you trying to increase our organic matter? Are you trying to put armor on the soil surface? Are you trying to improve water infiltration? And the list goes on and on. But before you start planting cover crops,
cues.zh: 你缺什么，就针对性地搭配种植什么覆盖作物。要知道，全国各地都在掀起一股覆盖作物热潮。但我见过很多由于缺乏合理规划而导致的种植灾难。你用覆盖作物到底想达成什么目的？是想增加有机质吗？是想给地表盖上一层“盔甲”吗？还是想提高水分入渗率？诸如此类。但在开始种植覆盖作物之前，

cues.en: You have to decide and determine what's my resource concern. What is it I'm trying to do? We have 2,000 acres of cropland. I honestly don't know how many fields. I haven't added it up. But we design cover crop mixes specifically for each field, because the resource concern will usually vary from field to field. So for instance, if you have the resource concern of a compaction layer, then you're going to use cover crops such as this is a
cues.zh: 你必须明确并决定：我的资源短板是什么？我究竟想达成什么？我们有 2,000 英亩耕地，老实说我甚至不知道分成了多少块地，没细算过。但我们会针对每块地专门设计覆盖作物的混播配方，因为不同地块面临的问题通常各不相同。比如，如果你的问题是土壤存在压实板结层，那你就要用专门的覆盖作物，比如像这种——

cues.en: daikon radish. And if you look down in that soil profile, there was a compaction layer down about 12 inches. Notice that radish, it tried growing down in the ground, hit that compaction layer, it comes back above ground until it gets enough energy to poke its way through. Radishes are also a nitrogen storage tank, so we use them in combination with legumes to sequester and store nitrogen for the next crop then. That's my
cues.zh: 白萝卜。如果你仔细看那处土壤剖面，在地下大概 12 英寸深的地方有一个板结层。注意看那个萝卜，它试图往深处扎根，碰到板结层后就往地表上拱，直到积蓄了足够的能量才扎透下去。萝卜还是个“氮素储存库”，所以我们把它们和豆科植物混种，用来固存氮素供下一茬作物吸收。那就是我的——

cues.en: fertilizer storage tank right there. These radishes can get really large. If you grow them, seed them a little later in the year. If you seed them in the spring, they're going to bolt and shoot a seed head, and they won't produce that big tuber. But they can get really big. This system that I'm talking with you about today can take place anywhere in the country. And I've got producers all over the world that are using this model, and Joel will talk about it later today too.
cues.zh: 化肥储存库。这些萝卜可以长得非常大。如果要种，记得在下半年播种。如果春天播种，它们就会抽薹结籽，长不出那么大的块根。但它们确实能长得极大。我今天跟各位分享的这套体系，在全国任何地方都适用。全世界都有农场主在采用这种模式，Joel 今天晚些时候也会讲到这一点。

cues.en: to produce a healthy ecosystem. This picture is of David Brandt, a friend of mine near Columbus, Ohio. David has been a no-tiller since 72, cover crops since 78. 2011 here, 225 bushel corn, zero. Synthetic inputs, zero herbicides, zero pesticides, zero fungicides. That's profitable. David likes to brag about the big radishes he grows. Him and I always have a contest, so I brag about my turnips.
cues.zh: 为了打造健康的生态系统。这张照片上是 David Brandt，我住在俄亥俄州 Columbus 附近的朋友。David 从 72 年起就搞免耕，78 年起种覆盖作物。这是 2011 年，玉米产量达到 225 蒲式耳，零合成投入品，零除草剂，零杀虫剂，零杀菌剂。这绝对是有利润的。David 喜欢吹嘘他种的大萝卜。我们俩总爱比一比，所以我就吹嘘我的芜菁。

cues.en: This is a partial list of the cover crops we grew on our ranch here this past year. Don't pay any attention to the species because that's gonna vary from area to area. But pay attention to what I've got here. I've got some species in all four crop types. Warm and cool season broad leaves and grasses. I'm using the cover crops to get diversity into my annual cropping system to build soil health.
cues.zh: 这是我们牧场过去一年种植的部分覆盖作物清单。不用太在意具体品种，因为各地情况会有所不同。但请注意我这里的配置：这四类作物我都涵盖了一些品种——暖季型和冷季型的阔叶植物与禾本科植物。我通过覆盖作物让一年生种植系统变得更加多样化，以此构建土壤健康。

cues.en: And that's what it's about. We're trying to address those resource concerns and build soil health. So I question the rationale of some things. My neighbor's not here today, so I can talk about him. I've been on that farm since 1983. His farm has directly crossed the road there from me. Every fall, he goes out and digs this little spot. It has done it every fall for 31 years.
cues.zh: 这就是核心所在。我们试图解决这些资源问题并构建土壤健康。所以我经常质疑某些做法的合理性。我邻居今天不在场，所以我可以聊聊他。我从 1983 年就一直在那个农场了。他的农场就在马路正对面。每年秋天，他都会跑去翻掘那块小地方。他连续 31 年每年秋天都这么干。

cues.en: This is a photo taken June 15th of 2009. I took it off the front deck of my house. The local weather service was forecasting a major rainfall event, which for us means anything over half an inch. But I took this photo. It started raining at 6.30 in the evening and by 12 midnight we had had 13.2 inches. This is a photo of the neighbor's dug area three weeks later.
cues.zh: 这是 2009 年 6 月 15 日拍的照片。我是在我家前廊上拍的。当地气象部门预报了一次强降雨过程，对我们来说，只要超过半英寸就算强降雨了。但我拍了这张照片。傍晚 6 点半开始下雨，到半夜 12 点，降雨量达到了 13.2 英寸。这是三周后邻居翻耕区域的照片。

cues.en: Still had water sitting there, and this happens every year. This photo here is my cropland directly across the road from his, immediately following, we had four tenths more inch of rain the next day, immediately following that 13.6 inches of rain. Do you see any erosion there? Now, I've got a little bit of bare soil in the foreground here where we, it did, when you get that much rain, it's gonna move a little of that residue away.
cues.zh: 水依然积在那里，而且年年如此。这张照片是我正对面的农田，紧接着第二天又下了 0.4 英寸的雨，就在那场 13.6 英寸的大雨之后。你能看出有任何水土流失吗？当然，前景这里有一点点裸露的土壤，毕竟雨量这么大，确实会冲走一点地表残茬。

cues.en: Jay Fier, our district conservationist, came out and took these photos. And he says, here's a photo of the soil that day, the morning after 13.6 inches. Jay makes the claim you could have drove a floater truck or any type of equipment over that field that day without rutting it up. Look at the soil aggregation. If you have those water infiltration pours, you're going to take that water down, then you're going to hold it in the soil profile for when you need it.
cues.zh: 我们地区的自然资源保护员 Jay Fier 过来拍了这些照片。他说，这是当天土壤的照片，就在那场 13.6 英寸降雨的次日早晨。Jay 坚称，那天你就算开着浮选卡车或任何设备驶过那片田，也不会压出车辙。看看这土壤团聚体。只要有这些渗水孔隙，水就会渗透下去，然后保存在土壤剖面中，以备不时之需。

cues.en: I mentioned when I started out in 1991, we could infiltrate a half of an inch per hour. 2011, last time NRCS come out and tested my soils, we can infiltrate over eight inches an hour now. I've never seen it rain, eight inches an hour. It's not how much moisture you get, it's how healthy are your soils. Can they infiltrate it and can they hold it and store it? That's what it's about. The fifth thing, animal impact.
cues.zh: 我提过，1991 年我刚起步时，每小时只能下渗半英寸水。到了 2011 年，NRCS 上次来检测我的土壤时，我们每小时的下渗量已经超过八英寸了。我从没见过一小时能下八英寸的雨。关键不在于你获得了多少水分，而在于你的土壤有多健康。它能渗透水分吗？能截留并储存起来吗？这才是核心所在。第五点，动物的影响。

cues.en: the fifth principle of building a healthy soil. I own this newspaper, The Prairie Farmer, from 1871, and it depicts the bison and the wolves following the bison, keeping them moving. How were soils formed? Soils were formed in conjunction with herbivores. Why don't we have that in agriculture today? We had these large herds of bison, et cetera, moving across the plains, and then we also had the local animals, the rabbits,
cues.zh: 构建健康土壤的第五条原则。我有一份1871年的《The Prairie Farmer》报纸，上面画着野牛，还有跟着野牛、让它们不断移动的狼。土壤是怎么形成的？土壤是与食草动物共同形成的。为什么今天的农业里没有这一环？过去有大批野牛等穿越平原，也有本地动物，比如兔子、

cues.en: grasshoppers, all these insects, they were taking this forage, the biomass, and cycling it through. Animals are an important part of a healthy ecosystem. Today, it's not uncommon to drive for thousands of miles and not even see a fence, let alone an animal. Why have we removed them from the ecosystem? And then we expect our soils to be healthy? Not going to happen.
cues.zh: 蚱蜢，所有这些昆虫，都在取食这些牧草和生物量，并把它循环起来。动物是健康生态系统的重要部分。今天，开上几千英里连栅栏都看不到，更别说动物了，这并不稀奇。为什么我们把它们从生态系统中移除了？然后还指望土壤健康？不可能。

cues.en: 2007, I was speaking at a conference in Brandon, Manitoba, and I got done speaking, and I had this guy in my face telling me that, boy, you see what I'm doing. And that was Neil Dennis from up there in Canada. And Neil's the mob grazer who puts up to a million head of livestock on an acre. I thought I was high stock density, running 200,000 to 300,000 pounds live weight per acre, until I met Neil.
cues.zh: 2007年，我在马尼托巴省布兰登市的一个会议上演讲。讲完后，有个人凑到我跟前说：老兄，你看看我在做什么。他就是加拿大那边的 Neil Dennis。Neil 是群牧放牧者，每英亩能放养多达一百万头牲畜。我原以为自己每英亩20万到30万磅活重的放牧密度已经很高了，直到遇到 Neil。

cues.en: Well, that next spring then, immediately I went up there and viewed his operation to see what he was doing. And the thing that amazed me is when we dug down in his soils, he was building more topsoil quicker than I was. And that bothers me, because I don't like to be second fiddle. But the important thing was that I could take a lesson from Neil. And I knew immediately that Neil was doing this on perennial
cues.zh: 于是第二年春天，我马上过去参观他的牧场运作，看看他在做什么。让我吃惊的是，我们挖开他的土壤时，他积累表土的速度比我快、量也比我多。这让我很不舒服，因为我不喜欢当第二。但重要的是，我能从 Neil 身上学到东西。我立刻明白，Neil 是在多年生

cues.en: pastures, and I understood that. But I needed to get more animal impact onto my cropland. That was the missing link in building soil health further on my cropland. So this is our ranch today. This isn't quite all of it. But the light blue areas are cropland. The light green areas are tame grass pastures. In other words, it was tilled at one time. And now it's ceded back to perennials. And then the yellow area is our perennial pastures.
cues.zh: 草场上做这件事，而且我明白这一点。但我需要让更多动物影响进入我的农田。那是我在农田上进一步提升土壤健康所缺的一环。这就是我们今天的牧场。这还不完全是我们牧场的全部。浅蓝色区域是农田，浅绿色区域是栽培草场。换句话说，它曾经被翻耕过，现在又恢复为多年生草地。黄色区域则是我们的多年生牧场。

cues.en: I mentioned we had three pastures starting out. We now have over 100 permanent pastures, but an infinite number of smaller ones. When we took over that operation, we could run 65 cow-calf pairs and about 35 yearlings. Today we're running 350 cow-calf pairs, 4 to 800 yearling and grass-finished cattle, plus some other livestock I'll talk to you about. But why I wanted to show you with this map is to show you that we're able to integrate all three of these. The perennial
cues.zh: 我提到过，我们一开始只有三块牧场。现在我们有一百多块永久牧场，还有无数更小的地块。我们接手那个经营体时，只能养65对带犊母牛和大约35头一岁牛。今天我们养着350对带犊母牛、400到800头一岁牛和草饲出栏牛，外加一些我稍后会讲的其他牲畜。我之所以想用这张地图给你们看，是想说明我们能把这三种都整合起来。多年生的

cues.en: natives, the perennial tame grass pastures, and the cropland. We integrate them all and graze livestock on all of them. Now, one of the easiest ways to get started into grazing animals on cropland is with fall-seated biannuals. This photo was taken here in early October. We had just harvested a crop and then went in there and seeded. In this case, it's a combination of winter triticale, a forage winter wheat, hairy vatch, sweet clover,
cues.zh: 原生草场、多年生栽培草场和农田。我们把它们全部整合起来，并在所有这些地块上放牧牲畜。现在，在农田上开始放牧牲畜最简单的方法之一，是种秋季播种的两年生作物。这张照片是十月初在这里拍的。我们刚收完一季作物，然后进去播种。这里混播了冬小黑麦、饲用冬小麦、毛叶苕子和草木樨，

cues.en: And there's some radish in there. And it's just poking through the ground there in October, even though we froze many, many, many times before that. So what we'll do then, we'll let that go. And then the next spring, we'll mob graze high stock densities on these high carbon biannuals. And we build very small paddocks. This photo I'm just using for illustration was taken on some tame grass pasture. But we'll go out there. And I don't care if you even have one animal, you can do high stock density grazing.
cues.zh: 里面还混了些萝卜。十月时它刚破土而出，尽管在那之前我们已经冻过很多很多次。那我们接下来会怎么做？先让它继续长。到第二年春天，我们会对这些高碳的两年生作物进行高密度群牧放牧。我们会围出很小的围栏小区。这张照片只是用来示意，是在某片栽培草场上拍的。但我们会到田里去实践。哪怕你只有一头牲畜，也能做高密度放牧。

cues.en: Just make your area small enough. That's all there is. So we'll go out there in the morning and we'll roll up the previous day's paddocks, set up the new days, takes about an hour. We'll use these bat latches in the lower left. Bat latches are a little solar powered gate opener. That's a bungee cord attached to them. We punch the time in. We want that to open. And then the livestock move themselves the rest of the day. So we don't have to be there.
cues.zh: 只要把区域划得足够小，就这么简单。所以我们早上会过去，收起前一天的围场，布置好新一天的围场，大约花一小时。我们用左下角这些 Bat latch。Bat latch 是一种小型太阳能开门器，上面连着弹力绳。我们设定好时间，让它到点打开。剩下的时间牲畜自己移动，我们不用在场。

cues.en: So when we're using this as a tool, and that's all mob grazing is, is it's a tool, just like no-till is a tool, cover crops are a tool, these are all tools, but we'll use that to address our resource concern. And in this particular case, where we're mob grazing these fall-seated biannuals, our resource concern is trying to get more armor on the soil surface. So we let that go, in order that cover crop get to a higher carbon state,
cues.zh: 所以当我们把它当工具用时——密集放牧也不过如此，它就是个工具，就像免耕是工具、覆盖作物是工具，这些都是工具——但我们用它来解决资源问题。在这个案例里，我们密集放牧这些秋播二年生植物，要解决的资源问题就是让土壤表面多一层覆盖。所以我们让它继续长，好让覆盖作物达到更高的碳状态，

cues.en: Now, obviously, for gain, if we wanted maximum gain on the livestock, we'd graze it, you know, when it's more immature. But we want the higher carbon state. There, the batlatch just opened, and in this particular photo, there's about 675,000 pounds of live weight per acre that are moving on to the next break. And there is what we're left with, that solid mat of carbon on the soil surface, the armor that's going to protect that soil.
cues.zh: 当然，如果追求牲畜最大增重，我们会在它更嫩的时候放牧。但我们想要更高的碳状态。看，Bat latch 刚打开；这张照片里，大约每英亩 67.5 万磅活重正移动到下一个围区。这就是我们留下的：土壤表面那层厚实的碳垫，也就是保护土壤的覆盖层。

cues.en: We only want the livestock to eat about a third of the above ground biomass. What happened when the herds of bison were moving across the Great Plains? Were they eating everything? No, they were trampling way more than they were eating. But it's that biomass on the soil surface that causes nutrient cycling, it's armored to protect the soil, preventing from the temperatures rising, it's preventing from wind erosion, and doing all these healthy things that occur in a healthy ecosystem.
cues.zh: 我们只想让牲畜吃掉约三分之一的地上生物量。当年野牛群在大平原上迁徙时是什么情况？它们把一切吃光了吗？没有，它们踩踏掉的远比吃掉的更多。但正是土壤表面的这些生物量促成养分循环，像铠甲一样保护土壤，防止温度升高，防止风蚀，并完成健康生态系统中所有这些有益的事。

cues.en: Then what we can do, this is a photo just three days later. So we were grazing this at a higher carbon state. It was already starting to form a seed head. So when we run those livestock on there, they trample it and it's going to die. And then I don't need a herbicide and I can go in there immediately and seed again. Now, our window growing season is not very long. I don't have time then to get a cash crop established, but I can certainly get another cover crop established in there.
cues.zh: 然后我们能做什么呢——这是仅仅三天后的照片。我们是在它碳状态更高时放牧的。它当时已经开始抽穗。所以把牲畜赶上去后，它们会踩踏它，它就会死掉。这样我就不需要除草剂，可以立刻进去再次播种。我们的生长季窗口并不长。我没时间再种一季经济作物，但完全可以在那里再建立一季覆盖作物。

cues.en: which is what we do. In this particular case, we're going in with a very diverse mix. It's during the warm time of the year, so we're primarily going to use warm season species, sorghum, sedan, millet, sunflowers, cowpeas, soybeans, that type of thing. I still add in some cool season species just because in case we get one of these cold fronts blowing through, which can happen, we'll have something that's able to cope with those temperatures. But look what I'm doing.
cues.zh: 我们就是这么做的。在这个案例里，我们播下非常多样的混合种。现在是一年中的温暖时期，所以我们主要用暖季品种：高粱、苏丹草、小米、向日葵、豇豆、大豆之类。我仍然会加一些冷季品种，因为万一有冷锋过境——这是可能发生的——我们也有能应对那些温度的品种。但看看我在做什么。

cues.en: with this amount of diversity. I'm really accelerating biological time. If I would seed these as monocultures, it'd take me 20 years to accomplish what I'm able to do in one year. Here's the seed just poking up through the soil surface. Notice that aggregation there. I don't like this photo. There's too much bare soil. But it does show how all these seeds seeded together at the same depth do just fine.
cues.zh: 有了这样的多样性。我确实在加速生物时间。如果我把这些作为单一作物播种，要花20年才能完成我一年就能做到的事。这是种子刚刚顶出土壤表面。注意那里的聚集。我不喜欢这张照片。裸露土壤太多了。但它确实展示了，所有这些种子在同一深度一起播种后长得很好。

cues.en: and they come up and grow just fine together. We're optimizing solar energy collection with these diverse cover crops. If you have a monoculture growing out there, how many leaf sizes and shapes do you have? One. No matter what direction that sun is from this field, I'm going to be harvesting solar energy. And that's what it's about for us as producers. We want to capture that soil energy, sequester it as carbon,
cues.zh: 它们一起出苗，长得很好。我们正用这些多样化的覆盖作物优化太阳能收集。如果你在那里种单一作物，你有多少种叶片大小和形状？一种。无论太阳从哪个方向照向这块地，我都能收获太阳能。对我们生产者来说，这就是关键。我们想捕获那些土壤能量，把它固存为碳，

cues.en: and start the nutrient cycle, feed soil biology. So if we get any moisture at all, this photo was taken with about two inches of moisture on it, and we can get some really good growth. Remember, my soil temps are kept lower. I don't evaporate down as deep. My soils are much more efficient water use wise than other soils. Then we have a lot of options with that cover crop. We tend to grass finish things so we can
cues.zh: 并启动养分循环，喂养土壤生物。所以只要我们有一点水分——这张照片是在大约两英寸水分时拍的——我们就能获得非常好的生长。记住，我的土壤温度保持得更低。我不会蒸发到那么深。我的土壤在水分利用方面比其他土壤高效得多。然后，我们对那种覆盖作物有很多选择。我们倾向于用草地育肥，这样我们可以

cues.en: We can turn some animals onto that warm season cover crop and grass finish. When we do that, we do not run near as high a stock density because we're shooting for maximum gain. We want those livestock gaining two and a half pounds a day and they'll do it on these warm season mixes. Or we can let it go and just let it continue to sequester carbon and to build biomass. And that's what it looks like then after a frost. Remember, extend the growing season. I used to think that, you know, our
cues.zh: 把一些牲畜放到那种暖季覆盖作物上，进行草地育肥。这样做时，我们不会采用那么高的载畜密度，因为我们追求最大增重。我们希望那些牲畜每天增重两磅半，而它们在这些暖季混合作物上能做到。或者我们可以放着不管，让它继续固碳并积累生物量。这就是霜冻之后的样子。记住，延长生长季。我以前以为，你知道，我们的

cues.en: Our average last frost in the spring is mid-May. First one comes in the fall, early September. I thought that narrow window was my growing season. As we've gotten a healthier soil, the biology in the soil keep the soil temperature warmer. We can easily grow species up until Thanksgiving, most years. Now, this year with the cold we've had, we're probably done for the year. Here's how we convert most of our cover crops to dollars, though.
cues.zh: 春季平均最后一次霜冻在五月中旬。秋季第一次霜冻在九月初。我以前以为那个狭窄的窗口就是我的生长季。随着土壤变得更健康，土壤中的生物让土壤温度更暖。大多数年份，我们可以轻松种植作物直到感恩节。现在，今年我们经历了寒冷，可能今年就到此为止了。不过，这就是我们把大部分覆盖作物变成美元的方式。

cues.en: We used to calve in February and March, which is the reason I have no hair, because it just doesn't work in North Dakota. We now calve in late May and June out on grass. We leave the calves on the cows all winter out there grazing. And they do just fine. The beauty of these cover crops is you can add so many different species and you can balance their rations. This calf here has eaten hairy vetch. Hairy vetch in December will still be 18% crude protein.
cues.zh: 我们过去在二月和三月产犊，这就是我没头发的原因，因为这在北达科他州根本行不通。我们现在在五月下旬和六月在草地上产犊。我们整个冬天把小牛留在母牛身边，让它们在那里放牧。它们长得很好。这些覆盖作物的妙处在于，你可以加入许多不同物种，并平衡它们的日粮。这里这头小牛吃过毛苕子。毛苕子在十二月仍然有18%的粗蛋白。

cues.en: Their nutritional needs are met by the cover crop. Why in the world would I want to go put up, hey, spend dollars? You know, we have a motto on our operation. We want to sign the back of the check and not the front. It's a pretty good motto. It leaves a lot more in your pocket. It does. It works good. It's a lot of fun, too. It allows me to come to Idaho when I should be, could be homework and feeding hay. I'll tell you a little story with this here. This fall,
cues.zh: 它们的营养需求由覆盖作物来满足。我到底为什么还要去收储干草、嘿，还要花钱呢？你知道，我们的经营有一条座右铭：我们要签支票的背面，而不是正面。这是条很好的座右铭。它让你口袋里留下更多钱。确实如此。效果很好。也很有乐趣。它让我能来爱达荷州，而本来我可能该去做作业、喂干草。我给你们讲个小故事。这个秋天，

cues.en: We had a father's son, they had heard about our operation, traveled up for a tour. And they were explaining their operation to me. They ran a thousand cow-calf pairs and then they backgrounded the calves. And they said, well, we got two hay machines, we put up hay. We got three balers. We got two semis to haul that hay home. And then in the winter, we start four tractors every day to feed those thousand cows and their calves. And they turned to my son and they asked him, well, what's your day like? And he says,
cues.zh: 有一对父子，他们听说了我们的经营方式，专程上来参观。然后他们向我介绍他们的经营。他们养了1000对母牛和犊牛，然后对小牛进行过渡饲养。他们说，嗯，我们有两台干草机，我们收储干草。我们有三台打捆机。我们有两辆半挂车把干草运回家。然后到了冬天，我们每天启动四台拖拉机，去喂那1000头母牛和它们的小牛。然后他们转向我儿子，问他，那你的一天是什么样的？他说，

cues.en: in the winter. And he says, well, I usually get up and make some coffee. And then I sit in the recliner and watch TV. He says, my biggest problem is I wear out too many recliners. Last year, we went at 350 cow-calf pairs. We started a tractor once. Animals have four legs for a reason. We don't need to provide them with a bed and breakfast. Let them find it on their own. And they prefer to do that. I honestly believe they're happier doing that than if we would confine them. When we start confining animals, we start
cues.zh: 在冬天。他说，嗯，我通常起床，煮点咖啡。然后坐在躺椅上看电视。他说，我最大的问题是把太多躺椅坐坏了。去年，我们养了350对母牛和犊牛。我们只启动过一次拖拉机。动物长四条腿是有原因的。我们不需要给它们提供床和早餐。让它们自己去找。而且它们更喜欢那样做。我真的相信，它们这样比我们把它们圈起来更快乐。当我们开始圈养动物，我们就开始

cues.en: causing more problems. And they can do it when it's real cold. That's not muskox. That's 350 cow-calf pairs grazing cover crops at over 40 degrees below zero. Actually felt a little sorry for my son as I sat in the pickup and he walked out and took this picture. But, you know, they're doing just fine and they survived just fine. Now, part of the problem is you got to make sure you have the type of cattle that can withstand those conditions. But we do by letting nature
cues.zh: 造成更多问题。而且它们能在非常冷的时候做到这一点。那不是麝牛。那是350对母牛和犊牛在零下40多度放牧覆盖作物。其实我坐在皮卡里，看着我儿子走出去拍这张照片，我还有点心疼他。但你知道，它们过得很好，也顺利活下来了。现在，部分问题在于，你得确保你有能承受那种条件的牛。但我们通过让自然

cues.en: make the selection. Then what we're able to do when we trample all that residue onto the soil surface, and remember, when we're grazing in the winter, it's just like in the summer, we don't want those livestock to eat all that. We want to trample residue, but we can build topsoil. This photo here, see where the blue lines are? That's the residue, the cover crop we trampled three years later. That's about three inches of new topsoil that we're building.
cues.zh: 做出选择。然后，当我们把那些残茬都踩踏到土壤表面时，我们能做的是——记住，冬天放牧时就像夏天一样，我们不想让那些牲畜把那些都吃光。我们想让它们踩踏残茬，但我们可以培育表土。这张照片，看到蓝线在哪里了吗？那是残茬，是我们三年前踩踏过的覆盖作物。那是我们正在培育的约三英寸厚的新表土。

cues.en: Now, I'm not going to call it all topsoil. It's biomass also. It's organic material laid down on top. But we're able to accelerate soil formation by using the principles of nature. Here's what I like to say. One-third for the critters above ground, two-thirds for those below ground. That's what it looks like in the spring then after we grazed one of these cover crops. We have that armor on the soil surface protecting the soil. I'm going to show you the fallacy
cues.zh: 现在，我不会把它全都叫作表土。它也是生物量。是铺在地表上的有机物质。但我们能够利用自然的原则来加速土壤形成。我喜欢这样说：三分之一给地上的生物，三分之二给地下的生物。这就是春天我们放牧过其中一块覆盖作物后的样子。土壤表面有那层盔甲保护着土壤。现在，我要给你们展示这个谬误

cues.en: of the current production model now. This particular field here, we went and took standard N, P, and K soil test. I know that's too small to read, but in the upper left it says pounds of nitrogen in the top 10 inches of soil, top, excuse me, two feet of soil profile is 10 pounds. How many bushel corn crop can you get off 10 pounds of N? Not much, I heard. I'll show you what I can do on 10 units of N.
cues.zh: 也就是当前生产模式的。这块地，我们去做了标准的氮、磷、钾土壤测试。我知道字太小看不清，但左上角写着：土壤表层10英寸，抱歉，是土壤剖面顶部2英尺内的氮含量是10磅。10磅氮能种出多少蒲式耳玉米？我听到有人说，不多。我给你们看看，用10个单位氮我能做到什么。

cues.en: Here we are planting into that residue. When I say I'm a no-tiller, I'm a no-tiller. On the left is planted, on the right is not. I don't use trash whippers. That's way too much tillage. Don't use row markers. Too much tillage. Okay? We don't want to disturb that armor. We want that protection there. Here's photos then. I plant corn about May 15th. Here's June 16th, July 1st. Where's the residue? I'm not out there cultivating. I'll tell you that.
cues.zh: 我们正直接播种到这些残茬里。我说我是免耕农，就真是彻彻底底的免耕。左边是播种过的，右边还没播。我不用清茬轮，那翻动土壤太厉害了。也不用划行器，翻耕太多了。明白吗？我们不想破坏这层地表覆盖，我们需要那层保护。来看这些照片，我大概在5月15日种玉米。这是6月16日，这是7月1日。残茬去哪儿了？我向你们保证，我可没下地中耕。

cues.en: Where's the residue going? Here's a photo of that same corn crop then at tasseling time. Dr. Ray Ward at Kearney, Nebraska. He owns Ward Labs. Him and I are friends. He used to think what I was doing was a bunch of hogwash. So he came up himself then and took these leaf tissue analysis of that corn. Every single nutrient he tested for was sufficient or above. I didn't add anything. We don't put on anything. We don't use foliars.
cues.zh: 残茬都去哪儿了？这是同一批玉米抽雄时的照片。内布拉斯加州卡尼的 Ray Ward 博士，他是 Ward Labs 的老板，我和他是朋友。他以前觉得我干的这些全是一堆鬼话。所以他亲自过来，对那些玉米做了叶片组织分析。他测定的每一种养分含量全都达标甚至过量。我可什么都没施。我们什么化肥都没用，也没用叶面肥。

cues.en: No amendments of any kind, certainly no synthetics. So I went from that soil test that showed I only had 10 units of end to a leaf tissue analysis that shows everything supplied that that plant needs. Where does it come from? There's what that field looked like in the fall then. All that residue is gone. It's consumed by soil life. I'm embarrassed to this photo. That's bare soil.
cues.zh: 没有任何改良剂，更别提合成制剂了。我的土壤检测原本显示只有10个单位的氮，而叶片组织分析却表明植物所需的一切都得到了充足供应。这到底是从哪儿来的？这就是那片地在秋天的样子。所有残茬都不见了，全被土壤生物消耗了。看到这张照片我挺惭愧的，那是裸露的土壤。

cues.en: That's why I grow, this was taken back in 2009. That's why I grow hairy vetch and other clovers with my corn now. Because I don't ever want anyone seeing bare soil on my operation. Not going to say it doesn't happen, but I'm certainly going to try my hardest to prevent it from happening. There's what we did. Now, county average in Burleigh County, North Dakota is just under 100 bushels. We got 142 bushel corn crop without adding any...
cues.zh: 这就是为什么——这张照片是2009年拍的——这就是为什么我现在种玉米要混种长柔毛野豌豆和其他三叶草。因为我绝不想让任何人在我的农场看到裸土。不敢说绝对不会发生，但我一定会竭尽全力去避免。这就是我们做的。现在，北达科他州伯利县的平均产量刚到100蒲式耳出头，而我们收获了142蒲式耳的玉米，而且没添加任何……

cues.en: No fertilizers, no pesticides, no fungicides, no herbicides in this field. My cost to produce a bushel of corn, market it, everything is $1.44 on this crop here. $1.44 a bushel. Today's corn price, I can still make money. We don't take part in government programs anymore. No crop insurance. I don't want to be encumbered by that, and I don't want to be on government welfare. So I just refuse to take part in government programs now.
cues.zh: 这片地里没用化肥、没用杀虫剂、没用杀菌剂，也没用除草剂。在这季作物上，我生产一蒲式耳玉米，算上推向市场等一切成本只要1.44美元。每蒲式耳1.44美元。按现在的玉米市价，我依然能大赚一笔。我们不再参与任何政府项目，也不买农作物保险。我不想受那些束缚，也不想吃政府补贴。所以我现在一概不参加政府项目。

cues.en: We can produce more at a lower cost in this type of production model. There's no doubt about it. The soil is alive if our management allows it to be. We have to start looking at healthy ecosystems and look at what the soil needs instead of what the plant needs. Soil without biology is just geology. The reason that soil test didn't work is it only took into account
cues.zh: 在这种生产模式下，我们能以更低的成本产出更多，这是毫无疑问的。只要管理得当，土壤就是活的。我们必须开始着眼于健康的生态系统，关注土壤需要什么，而不是只看作物需要什么。没有生物的土壤，充其量只是地质岩石。之前土壤测试失灵的原因在于，它只考虑了

cues.en: the chemical and physical properties of the soil. It did not take into account all the biology that I have in my healthy soils. This gentleman here, Dr. Richard Haney at Temple, Texas, has developed a new soil test that I think will really help link the conventional production model into the more biological production model. You send a soil test in there, and Dr. Haney is measuring things like water extractable organic carbon, which is what the biology eats,
cues.zh: 土壤的化学和物理特性。它根本没有考虑到我健康土壤中的所有生物成分。这位先生是德克萨斯州坦普尔的 Richard Haney 博士，他开发出了一种新的土壤测试法，我认为这能真正将传统生产模式与更具活力的生物生产模式连接起来。把土样送过去，Haney 博士会检测水溶性有机碳等指标，而这正是土壤微生物的养料，

cues.en: And he's able to extrapolate and determine how much nutrients can you get out of your soil due to the biology, the chemical, and the physical properties. This new soil test will revolutionize soil testing in North America. There's no doubt in my mind it's being used. There's like six labs now. Ward Labs is one of them that does this soil test. Cost about $50 to do a test.
cues.zh: 他能够借此推断并测算出，结合生物、化学和物理特性，土壤究竟能为你释放多少养分。这种新型土壤测试将彻底颠覆北美的土壤检测。毫无疑问它正在推广普及，目前大概有六家实验室，Ward Labs 就是能做这种测试的其中之一，做一次大约需要50美元。

cues.en: But that'll be the link that can show producers how much they can start cutting back on their synthetics, if they are using synthetics. Now, what about livestock onto soils? You know, the impact of livestock on cropland. For years, I was told, Gabe, your system's going to crash, you're going to run out of phosphorus and potassium. Nitrogen's a no-brainer. Above every acre of land, we have about 34,000 tons of atmospheric nitrogen.
cues.zh: 但这会成为关键纽带，让农户明白如果在使用化学合成物，究竟能减少多少用量。那么，把牲畜引入土壤又会怎样？也就是牲畜对农田的影响。多年来总有人跟我说：Gabe，你的系统迟早要崩溃，你的磷和钾迟早会耗尽。氮素倒不用愁。在每英亩土地的上空，都存在大约 34,000 吨的大气氮。

cues.en: I don't know why anyone would want to write a check for nitrogen when it's free. All you got to do is plant legumes. It just makes no sense to me. So we're not going to pay attention. Over on the left, that's nitrogen. We're not going to pay much attention to that. What this is here is this is comparing two of my fields. They both have been no-tilled a long time. They both have had very diverse crop rotations. They both have had cover crops. The only difference is the green barred field has had
cues.zh: 明明是免费的，我真不懂为什么还会有人花钱买氮肥。只要种豆科植物就行了，我实在理解不了。所以这里我们先跳过。左边那一项是氮，我们不用太在意。这里对比的是我的两块田地。它们都长期采用免耕，都进行了高度多样化的轮作，也都有种植覆盖作物。唯一的区别是，绿条代表的那块田地已经……

cues.en: livestock integration two of the past six years. Nitrogen's about the same there, 86 to 90 pounds. The second bar there is inorganic phosphorus. In other words, what's available to the plant. We jumped from 65 pounds to 239 pounds. Now, how did that happen? You know, those livestock didn't bring any phosphorus with them. But what this shows is the importance of herbivores grazing on the land.
cues.zh: 过去六年中有两年结合了牲畜放牧。那里的氮含量基本持平，在 86 到 90 磅。那里的第二个柱状图代表无机磷。换句话说，就是植物可以直接利用的磷。我们直接从 65 磅暴增到了 239 磅。那么，这是怎么发生的呢？要知道，那些牲畜可没有自带任何磷。但这充分说明了草食动物在土地上放牧的重要性。

cues.en: Because they're grazing a living crop, that crop then, cover crop, is able to secrete more root exudates, break down more of that organic phosphorus so it can cycle through to the plants. Nature had this all figured out for thousands of years just that we forgot about it with our stupid industrial farming model. We need to get back to the principles of nature. The third bar there is potassium, same thing, significant increase.
cues.zh: 因为它们啃食的是活体作物，而这种覆盖作物就能分泌更多根系分泌物，分解更多有机磷，使其循环供给植物。大自然几千年来早就把这一切安排明白了，只是我们那套愚蠢的工业化农业模式把它忘了。我们需要回归自然的原则。那里的第三根柱是钾，同样，显著增加。

cues.en: When we start following the principles of nature, nature takes care of all this. It's so much more fun not having to write a check for this stuff now, you know? Now, I'm not going to tell you that there's not areas where there's blatant deficiencies in a nutrient, and you're not going to get this overnight. But I know one thing, there's thousands of producers using this model all over the world. It'll work anywhere. We've had visitors to our operations from all 50 states and 16 foreign countries now.
cues.zh: 当我们开始遵循自然规律时，大自然就会把这一切都处理好。现在不用再为这些东西掏钱，真的有趣多了，你懂吧？我不是说没有某些地方存在某种养分明显不足的情况，而且这也不是一夜之间就能实现的。但我知道一件事：全世界有成千上万的生产者在使用这个模式。它在哪儿都行得通。现在已经有来自全美50个州和16个外国的访客来过我们的农场。

cues.en: I've had groups from South Africa and England and Denmark and Australia who are all doing the same thing. I haven't found anywhere in the world where there's production agriculture that this model won't work because it's simply the model that nature provided. My son took this photo a few years back and I just love it. That's our cattle in the foreground, that's the neighbor in the background, which is going to put more dollars in your pocket. Here's a young man who first heard Ray Archuleta and I speak four years ago, Michael Thompson down in Kansas.
cues.zh: 我接待过来自南非、英国、丹麦和澳大利亚的团队，他们都在做同样的事。我在世界上还没找到哪个商业化农业生产的地方用不了这个模式，因为它就是大自然提供的模式。这张照片是我儿子几年前拍的，我特别喜欢。前景是我们的牛，背景是邻居的，这会让你多赚些钱。这位年轻人四年前第一次听 Ray Archuleta 和我演讲，他是堪萨斯州的 Michael Thompson。

cues.en: His dad was pretty hesitant, and he says, well, Michael, I'll tell you this much. We'll take that field. I'm going to farm half of it my way. You farm half of it your way. This is after four years. Look at the difference in soils. That's Michael's on the left. That's his father's half of the field on the right. Which one has more carbon? Which one has higher organic matter? Which one has more soil life? Which one has more aggregation, more infiltration? That's an amazing photo.
cues.zh: 他父亲挺犹豫，他说，好吧，Michael，我就跟你说这么多。我们拿那块地。我按我的方式种一半。你按你的方式种一半。这是四年之后。看看土壤的差别。左边是 Michael 的。右边是他父亲种的那一半地。哪边碳更多？哪边有机质更高？哪边土壤生物更丰富？哪边团聚体更多、入渗更好？这张照片太惊人了。

cues.en: We can change soils in a very short time with diversity, animal impact. It works. We've seen a real upward trend in organic matter levels on our operation. I mentioned we were less than 2% when we started. We're 5.3 to 6.1% now. And this has taken me a lot of years to learn all these things. I'm a slow learner. But guys like Michael, who try things a lot faster than I did, they're going to make even more rapid advances.
cues.zh: 通过多样性、牲畜影响，我们能在很短时间内改变土壤。这确实有效。在我们的农场中，有机质水平出现了明显的上升趋势。我提到过，开始时我们不到 2%。现在我们是 5.3% 到 6.1%。我花了很多年才学会所有这些。我学得慢。但像 Michael 这样的人，尝试新东西比我快得多，他们会取得更快的进展。

cues.en: Now, what's the value of that? Take a look at organic matter levels, and then you can start extrapolating out the amount of nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, sulfur in your soils. A 1% organic matter soils has about $751 per acre of those nutrients in it. My 5% organic matter soils, I'm over $3700 of nutrients in there. Back when I used to use it, you have to use a banker.
cues.zh: 那么，这值多少钱？看看有机质水平，你就能开始推算土壤中氮、磷、钾、硫的含量。有机质为 1% 的土壤，每英亩约含价值 751 美元的这些养分。我的土壤有机质为 5%，其中养分价值超过 3700 美元。以前我用这套办法时，你得找银行家。

cues.en: I went to him and I said, I want to put that on my balance sheet. And he said, well, I can't do that. And I said, why? You allow Joe to prepay fertilizer, put it on there. He says, you got a point. Now I no longer use a banker, and it's a lot more fun. Now, in your dry environment here, I'm going to run through this little analogy, the importance of water holding capacity of soils. When I started out, I have silt loam soils, so the middle column there.
cues.zh: 我去找他，说我想把这个记到我的资产负债表上。他说，不行，我不能这么做。我说，为什么？你允许 Joe 预付肥料款，把它记上去。他说，你说得有道理。现在我不再找银行家了，这有趣多了。现在，在你们这里干旱的环境中，我要用这个小类比说明土壤持水能力的重要性。我开始的时候，土壤是粉砂壤土，就是中间那一列。

cues.en: Less than two percent organic matter, I could only hold a little under two inches of moisture per foot of the soil profile. So in a four foot soil profile, I could hold a little under eight inches of water. Today I'm well over five percent, I can hold over 20 inches of water. We only get 15 inches on the average per year. I can hold all the moisture that falls on our operation. It's not how much moisture you get, it's how much you use.
cues.zh: 有机质不到 2% 时，每英尺土壤剖面我只能保住略低于 2 英寸的水分。所以在 4 英尺土壤剖面中，我只能保住略低于 8 英寸的水。如今我远超 5%，能保住超过 20 英寸的水。我们这里平均每年只有 15 英寸降水。我能保住落在我们农场上的所有水分。关键不是你得到多少水，而是你用了多少。

cues.en: Two weeks ago, I was in southeastern Missouri in the Delta region. They get over 50 inches of annual precipitation, and they're applying 50 inches plus of irrigated water to produce 200 bushel corn. While I put together a slide, I showed you my yields, I'm producing about just under nine and a half bushels of corn per inch of water. They were producing barely two.
cues.zh: 两周前，我在密苏里州东南部的三角洲地区。那里年降水量超过 50 英寸，他们还要施用 50 英寸以上的灌溉水，来生产 200 蒲式耳玉米。我做了张幻灯片，给你们看我的产量：我大约每英寸水生产略低于 9.5 蒲式耳玉米。他们每英寸水只能生产勉强 2 蒲式耳。

cues.en: I showed them. I said, if you had my water use efficiency, you'd be producing 950 bushel corn, right? Very inefficient system they have. It doesn't make sense. They cannot compete production-wise with what we can do with healthy soils. OK, so for 1% organic matter in the top six inches of the soil profile, you'll hold about 27,000 gallons of water. These are approximately OK. There's a few variables in there.
cues.zh: 我给他们算了笔账。我说，如果你们的水分利用效率能达到我这种水平，每英亩就能产950蒲式耳玉米，对吧？他们的系统效率非常低，根本说不通。在产量上，他们根本没法跟我们用健康土壤做出的成绩相比。在土壤表层6英寸的剖面中，有机质每增加1%，就能涵养大约27,000加仑的水。这只是个大概估算，里面还有一些变量。

cues.en: So, in 1993, when I started, our 5,000-acre ranch, we could hold 256,500,000 gallons of water. That sounds like a lot, but today, we can hold over 810 million gallons of water. That's huge. Think of the ramifications. Now, let's carry that out even further. Understand there's a reservoir called Hubbard Reservoir near you. It's 4,060-acre feet.
cues.zh: 在1993年我刚起步时，我们5,000英亩的牧场只能涵养2亿5650万加仑的水。听起来不少，但现在，我们能涵养超过8.1亿加仑的水。这个数字非常惊人，想想这背后的影响。我们再进一步对比一下，你们附近有个叫 Hubbard Reservoir 的水库，蓄水量是4,060英亩-英尺。

cues.en: It'll hold about 1,322,955,000 gallons of water. At the rate we're improving our organic matter on our farm, we're going to be over 10% pretty soon. In other words, our 5,000 acre ranch will hold more water than the Hubbard Reservoir will. That's the potential each of you as producers have. I don't care what scale you're talking about, whether you're talking about a quarter acre urban vegetable farm,
cues.zh: 它大概能蓄水13亿2295.5万加仑。按照我们农场改善土壤有机质的速度，我们很快就会超过10%。换句话说，我们这5,000英亩牧场的蓄水量将超过 Hubbard Reservoir 水库。这就是你们每位种植者所具备的潜力。不管你的规模有多大，哪怕只是四分之一英亩的城市菜园，

cues.en: or whether you're talking a large ranch, the water holding capacity is up to you. Don't blame it on drought or how much rain falls. We all have the ability to change our soils. Soil carbon, then, is the key driver for the nutritional status of plants, and it is the key driver for moisture holding capacity. In other words, soil carbon is the key driver for farm profit. Any farm you go on, that's going to be the key driver for farm profit.
cues.zh: 还是大面积的牧场，蓄水能力都取决于你自己。别总怪干旱，也别怪降雨量少。我们都有能力改变自己的土壤。因此，土壤碳是决定植物营养状况的核心驱动力，也是保水能力的关键驱动力。换句话说，土壤碳就是农场盈利的核心驱动力。无论你去哪家农场，这都是农场能否盈利的关键。

cues.en: All living things are based on carbon. We have to start thinking of our operations in terms of carbon. I'm going to show you now, just if you don't think I'm crazy by now, I'm going to prove it to you. Me and David Brandt, who I showed you a picture of, and Gail Fuller down in Kansas, we have a contest every year to see who can do the craziest thing. Well, I got thinking about cover crops, and then I got thinking about my garden.
cues.zh: 所有生命都以碳为基础。我们必须开始从碳的角度来规划生产运营。我现在就展示给你们看——要是你们现在还没觉得我疯了，那我证明给你们看。我和照片里给你们看过的 David Brandt，还有堪萨斯的 Gail Fuller，我们每年都比赛看谁做的事最疯狂。当时我一直在琢磨覆盖作物，接着又想到了我的菜园。

cues.en: First, I'll talk a little bit about, I had some potato growers there and they said, Gabe, it's all well and good you're doing, but we're potatoes growers, we can't do it no-till. So I thought about that one winter. So this is my no-till potatoes. We lay down a little layer of compost and you can see the potato seed, we just lay it on top. Then we fire up a tractor, roll around bale of alfalfa hay over it, come back in the fall, peel back the alfalfa hay, and there's our potatoes. We can do it no-till.
cues.zh: 首先我聊聊这个，之前有些土豆种植户对我说：“Gabe，你做的事确实很好，但我们是种土豆的，根本不可能免耕。”于是一年冬天我就琢磨起这事来。这就是我的免耕土豆：我们先铺上一薄层堆肥，你们可以看到种薯，直接放在上面就行。然后我们开动拖拉机，把一捆捆紫花苜蓿干草滚压在上面；等到秋天回来，掀开苜蓿干草，土豆就在那儿。我们完全可以做到免耕种植。

cues.en: It's easy, it works good. You've got to be a little careful with the thickness of the hay. Potatoes aren't going to be quite as large, but it's sure a lot easier to pick potatoes this way. And they're clean, and they're healthy. Now, what I did for the garden was we just took 30 species of vegetables, 20 species of annual flowers, 20 species of cover crop seed, mixed them all together, put them in the drill, and seeded 30 acres. That's our garden.
cues.zh: 很简单，效果也不错。干草厚度得稍微注意点。土豆不会那么大，但这样收土豆确实容易多了。而且干净、健康。至于菜园，我是这么做的：拿30种蔬菜、20种一年生花卉、20种覆盖作物种子，全混在一起，放进播种机，播了30英亩。那就是我们的菜园。

cues.en: It was absolutely fantastic. The wife had asked me, what do you want for supper? Whatever I tripped over, that's what we were eating. In the middle there, that's the potatoes we harvested. You know, we're dry land, don't have any water, you know, any moisture to irrigate with, but we don't have to because we're taking advantage of the biology in the soils and the natural ecosystem in the soils, the mycorrhizal fungi moving those nutrients and that water.
cues.zh: 简直太棒了。妻子问我晚饭想吃什么？我在地里绊到什么，晚饭就吃什么。中间那堆就是我们收的土豆。你知道，我们是旱地，没有水，也没有可灌溉的水分，但没必要，因为我们利用土壤里的生物学和自然生态系统，靠菌根真菌运送那些养分和水分。

cues.en: Works fantastic. We took all we wanted and then donated the rest to needy families and it's a good project. Then after that we ran the grass-finished beef on there, we ran the poultry on there, worked extremely well. We're stacking enterprises. Vandana Shiva said this, in nature's economy the currency is not money, it is life. So think of what I was doing when I had this 70 species mix, I'm adding as much life as possible to those soils.
cues.zh: 效果非常好。我们拿够了，剩下的捐给困难家庭，这是个好项目。之后我们在上面养草饲肉牛，养家禽，效果极好。我们在叠加经营项目。Vandana Shiva说过，在自然经济中，货币不是钱，而是生命。所以想想我做的：用这70种混合种子，我是在给那些土壤尽可能多地增加生命。

cues.en: I had as much biological impact on those soils in one year as it would, if I would have, it would have took 70 years if I would have planted them all as monocultures. We're accelerating biological time. That's all we're doing. On our operation then, it's about feeding the whole. We want to feed everything. We don't look at everything as independent. One of the things we do is we spend a lot of time paying attention to insects.
cues.zh: 我对那些土壤一年产生的生物影响，相当于如果我把它们全作为单一栽培来种，要花70年才能达到。我们在加速生物时间。我们做的就是这件事。在我们的经营中，关键是滋养整个系统。我们想喂养一切。我们不把一切看作彼此独立。我们做的事之一，就是花很多时间关注昆虫。

cues.en: On all the cover crops and annual crops we grow, we want species flowering at all times because they're going to attract both the pollinator insects and the predator insects. I mentioned that I haven't used an insecticide since before the turn of the century. There's no need because we give a home to all the predator insects. They're going to take care of all the pests.
cues.zh: 在我们种的所有覆盖作物和一年生作物上，我们希望任何时候都有物种在开花，因为它们会吸引传粉昆虫和捕食性昆虫。我提到过，世纪之交以前我就没用过杀虫剂了。没必要，因为我们给所有捕食性昆虫提供了家。它们会处理掉所有害虫。

cues.en: Good friend of mine, Dr. Jonathan Lundgren, he's an entomologist at ARS in Brookings, South Dakota, told me this. For every one insect species that's a pest, there's 1,700 that are either beneficial or indifferent. So as producers, we're focused on killing that one pest. Meanwhile, we're killing everything else that could take care of that one pest. Makes absolutely no sense. Sign the back of the check, not the front. We also have to focus on the life in the soil.
cues.zh: 我的好朋友Dr. Jonathan Lundgren，是南达科他州Brookings的ARS昆虫学家，他告诉我：每有一种害虫昆虫，就有1700种是有益或无害的。所以作为生产者，我们一心要杀死那一种害虫。同时，我们也在杀死其他所有本可以对付那一种害虫的东西。这完全说不通。在支票背面签名，而不是正面。我们还必须关注土壤里的生命。

cues.en: all that biology that's in the soil because that's what drives nutrient cycling. We also have a tremendous amount of wildlife on our operation. We're located now in city jurisdiction. The city of Bismarck is one of the fastest growing metropolitan areas in the U.S. We have a huge wildlife population on our ranch. The wildlife knows where they have a healthy home.
cues.zh: 还有土壤里的那些生物，因为正是它们驱动养分循环。我们的农场里也有大量野生动物。我们现在位于城市管辖范围内。Bismarck 是美国发展最快的大都市区之一。我们牧场上有庞大的野生动物种群。野生动物知道哪里有健康的家园。

cues.en: Now, I'm not going to get into livestock very much today. I'm going to speed through this on account of time. But on our operation, we run 350 cow-calf pairs. We have 4 to 800 stocker cattle, along with grass-finished beef. And then we also have a U-flock, and we're raising grass-finished lambs. We run these together to try and mimic the native ecosystem.
cues.zh: 今天我不太会深入讲畜牧。因为时间关系，这部分我会快速带过。但在我们的经营中，我们养了 350 对母牛-犊牛。我们有 400 到 800 头育成牛，还有草饲育肥牛肉。然后我们还有一群母羊，在养草饲育肥羔羊。我们把它们一起放养，尽量模拟本地生态系统。

cues.en: what it was. You know, there's no longer bison where we're at. My neighbors would get upset if bison were drinking out of their swimming pool, so I gotta mimic that how I can. So we have cattle, we have sheep, we have broilers. Now, we're limited a little bit. There is no slaughter facility in North or South Dakota, so they limit us to 999 broilers, which is about as many as my son can talk his mom and dad into helping him butcher.
cues.zh: 也就是它原来的样子。你知道，我们那儿已经没有野牛了。要是野牛喝邻居游泳池里的水，邻居会不高兴，所以我只能尽量模拟那种生态。于是我们养牛、养羊、养肉鸡。现在我们受到一点限制。北达科他州和南达科他州都没有屠宰场，所以他们把我们的肉鸡数量限制在 999 只，这差不多是我儿子能说服爸妈帮他宰杀的最大数量。

cues.en: But we run those broilers then out on these cover crops. Works extremely well. I laugh today. People are talking about the high price of calves, you know, and they're getting $3, $3.50 a pound for calves. My son gets $5 a pound for broilers, you know. That is the most profitable enterprise on our operation right now. He also has layers. This is Paul's version of Joel's Eggmobile. Paul takes these old stock trailers.
cues.zh: 但我们把这些肉鸡放到覆盖作物上放养。效果非常好。我今天还想笑。大家在说小牛价格高，你知道，小牛能卖到每磅 3 美元、3.5 美元。我儿子养的肉鸡能卖到每磅 5 美元。那是我们农场目前最赚钱的业务。他还养蛋鸡。这是 Paul 版的 Joel's Eggmobile。Paul 会把这些旧牲畜拖车……

cues.en: and he tears the floor out of them, puts wire mesh in them, an S-box, and we pull them around where we have the grass-finished animals, and they take care of the fly problems. Spread that cattle manure out. Works fantastic. It's taking advantage of what would occur in a natural ecosystem. We also have pastured pork. We farrow our own and then raise the pigs out and sell pastured pork. We produce a lot of grain.
cues.zh: 他把车厢地板拆掉，装上铁丝网，再加一个 S-box，然后我们把这些拖车拉到草饲育肥动物所在的地方，它们就能解决苍蝇问题，把牛粪摊开。效果特别好。这是在利用自然生态系统中本来会发生的事。我们还做放牧猪肉。我们自己繁育母猪产仔，再把猪养大，出售放牧猪肉。我们生产很多谷物。

cues.en: We prefer to market it through the hogs, a little bit through the chickens. Most of our grain gets sold to other producers who want to buy healthy grains. We've been non-GMO now for six years, seven years, something like that. We're not certified organic simply because I don't believe I should have to pay somebody to certify what I already know. We prefer to self-certify. Our ranch is open to our customers at all times. They can come any time they want and see what we're doing.
cues.zh: 我们更愿意通过猪来销售这些谷物，少量通过鸡。我们的大部分谷物卖给其他想买健康谷物的生产者。我们已经做了六七年非转基因，差不多这么久。我们没有做有机认证，只是因为我觉得没必要花钱让别人来认证我已经知道的事。我们更愿意自我认证。我们的牧场随时对客户开放。他们想什么时候来就什么时候来，看看我们在做什么。

cues.en: What we're trying to do with all these species then is to harvest different levels of energy. You know, Pete made a point about feeding 9 billion people by the year 2050. In this type of a production model, it is absolutely no problem. I'm producing cash grains and I've got all these different other enterprises on top of that. I will produce way more calories per acre than any standard conventional production model of monocultures.
cues.zh: 我们想用所有这些物种做的，就是收获不同层次的能量。你知道，Pete 提到过到 2050 年养活 90 亿人。在这种生产模式下，那绝对没问题。我在生产商品谷物，而且在此基础上还有所有这些不同的经营项目。我每英亩产生的热量会远远超过任何标准的单一化常规生产模式。

cues.en: There's no way they can produce as many calories per acre as I can. Feeding the world is no problem if we change our mindset. So, what we're doing on our operation is we're stacking all of these enterprises. And, you know, there's an infinite number of possibilities out there, and I know Joel will talk a lot more about that. I could care less, really, what happens to the price of individual commodities.
cues.zh: 他们每英亩产出的热量绝不可能比我多。只要转变观念，养活全世界根本不成问题。所以在我们农场里，我们把所有这些业务形态叠加在一起。你看，这其中有无数种可能，我知道 Joel 接下来会详细讲这点。至于单一农产品价格怎么变，我其实根本不在乎。

cues.en: As I mentioned, I was speaking in Missouri a couple weeks ago. Boy, those boys are tied into the price of corn and beans. I said, if you have a system that has multiple enterprises, doesn't matter. We're always going to have something that's profitable, because we're taking advantage of the efficiencies of nature. We, as producers, must also remember that we are in the business of producing nutrition. Our decisions greatly affect human health.
cues.zh: 就像我刚才提到的，几周前我去密苏里州演讲。天哪，那群家伙完全被玉米和大豆的价格绑死了。我说，如果你有一套多元化的业务体系，价格波动就无所谓了。我们总能赚到钱，因为我们在利用大自然本身的效率。作为生产者，我们还必须牢记，我们做的是生产营养的生意。我们的决定极大地影响着人类的健康。

cues.en: You know, the United States spends more on health care than any other country in the world, yet we're the 42nd healthiest country in the world. We're first in cancer, ADD, ADHD, Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, autoimmune diseases, obesity, and the list goes on and on. Why is that? I'm not going to blame it all on producers, don't get me wrong, but we as producers have to take our share of the blame for that. We have to start focusing on producing nutrition instead of just yield.
cues.zh: 你知道，美国在医疗保健上的支出比世界上任何国家都多，但健康程度却仅排在第42位。我们在癌症、ADD、ADHD、帕金森病、阿尔茨海默病、自身免疫性疾病、肥胖症等各个方面都高居榜首，名单还在不断变长。为什么会这样？别误会，我并不是把责任全推给生产者，但作为生产者，我们必须承担属于我们的那份责任。我们必须开始专注于生产营养，而不仅仅是追求产量。

cues.en: Here's a photo my son took. That's our pastured egg on the right. That's a conventional store one on the left. You analyze those ones. You're going to be amazed at the difference. That's one thing we're really focused on our operation now is tying soil health into human health. We're starting to do a lot of nutrient testing of the products we're producing so we can back up that statement. In North Dakota, there was only three processing plants in the state.
cues.zh: 这是我儿子拍的一张照片。右边是我们牧场放养的鸡蛋，左边是普通超市里买的。你去做个分析，两者的差距会让你大吃一惊。我们在农场运营中真正聚焦的一点，就是将土壤健康与人类健康联系起来。我们正在对自己生产的产品进行大量的营养成分检测，以此来证实这一观点。在北达科他州，全州只有三家加工厂。

cues.en: The waiting list to get an animal processed was over a year. So a group of us got together, and we opened this meat processing facility in January. So now we have our own abattoir where we can process. That way, we can direct market all of our products. So we're direct marketing. We're trying to direct market everything we produce on our operation. That's our own trademark logo, nourished by nature, because that's what we're trying to do.
cues.zh: 牲畜送去屠宰加工的排队时间要一年以上。于是我们几个人合伙，在今年一月份开了一家肉类加工厂。现在我们有了自己的屠宰场来进行加工。这样一来，我们就可以直销所有产品了。所以我们做直销，尽量把农场生产的所有东西都直接卖给消费者。那是我们的商标 logo，“自然滋养（nourished by nature）”，因为这就是我们在做的事。

cues.en: We're trying to provide nutrition to people through the natural ecosystems. Here's our meat trailer. We're direct marketing to consumers. We thought we were pretty isolated in Bismarck, North Dakota there. We can't even begin to keep up with demand right now. We never expected the onslaught that we received. There's nothing more gratifying than handing somebody a steak. They give you $20 a pound and they thank you for it. That is a good feeling.
cues.zh: 我们正尝试通过自然生态系统为人们提供营养。这是我们的冷藏肉类拖车。我们直接面向消费者销售。原本我们以为北达科他州的 Bismarck 挺偏远的。结果现在需求旺盛到我们根本供不应求。完全没想到会迎来如此火爆的抢购潮。没有什么比亲手递给顾客一块牛排更让人满足的了。他们按每磅20美元付钱给你，还要向你道谢。这种感觉真的很棒。

cues.en: You know, I can live with that. So here's what we've done on our operation. Starting on the left, in 1993, we had shallow soils, 1.7% organic matter. We started to no-till. Then we, in 95, we started to diversify the cash crop rotation. We noticed an uptick in our organic matter. 1997, we really started focusing on cover crops and how do we get cover crops on all of our cropland acres. Another jump in soil health.
cues.zh: 其实这完全可以接受。下面就是我们农场这些年的实践。从左边开始看，1993 年时土壤很薄，有机质只有 1.7%。我们开始推行免耕。到了 95 年，我们开始尝试经济作物多样化轮作，并发现有机质有所回升。1997 年，我们开始把重点放在覆盖作物上，琢磨如何让所有耕地都种上覆盖作物。土壤健康状况随之又实现了一次跃升。

cues.en: 2006 then, we really started planting the multi-species cover crops, and then we started adding mob grazing and integrating all these different livestock species on the land. Each one of those things we did, we saw a marked improvement in the health of our land, in the health of the ecosystem, in the water holding capacity. And now here in 2013,
cues.zh: 到了 2006 年，我们真正开始种植多样化覆盖作物，接着引入了高密度轮牧，把各种牲畜都整合到了土地上。我们采取的每一项措施，都带来了土地健康、生态系统健康以及土壤保水能力的显著改善。而到了 2013 年，

cues.en: We have a plot of land that we've now risen to 11.1% organic matter using these principles. We can improve soil health much, much faster than we used to think possible. It's just a matter of following the principles of nature. If you have healthy soil, you're gonna have clean water, you're gonna have clean air, you're gonna have healthy plants, healthy animals, and healthy people. And that's what it's about on our operation. How do we produce a healthy ecosystem?
cues.zh: 通过遵循这些原则，我们的一块土地有机质已经提升到了 11.1%。改善土壤健康的速度，远比我们过去想象的要快得多。关键就在于遵循自然规律。拥有了健康的土壤，就会有干净的水、清新的空气，以及健康的植物、动物和人类。这就是我们农场所追求的：我们该如何打造健康的生态系统，

cues.en: and equate it to healthy humans. So, with that, there's my contact information. Feel free to contact me or my son at any time. I'll be happy to visit with you.
cues.zh: 并最终转化为人类的健康。好了，上面是我的联系方式。欢迎随时联系我和我儿子，非常期待与大家交流。
